newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crudes slightly weaker, follow futures.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes slightly weaker, follow futures.

text.p: Crude oil prices in Asia were slightly weaker on Thursday in line with overnight futures markets, which tempered the rise in light sweet grades.
A producer has sold more than 2.5 million barrels of Tapis in November -- at prices as high as $1.20. It is already marketing December Tapis at a premium of $1.30.
Traders are waiting for the result of a tender by Burma to buy November crude for an update on Tapis values.
Traders said a cargo of Minas was traded into China at premiums above 20 cents, slightly higher than recent deals done at 20 cents premium.
An equity producer said it was offering Minas for the November market at a premium of 35 cents and expected healthy demand owing to the wide Brent/Dubai which is keeping West African crude sidelined.
The December Brent/Dubai was assessed at $2.40/$2.50 per barrel, little changed from the day-earlier $2.43/$2.50.

Dubai intermonth spreads were assessed around 50 cents for near-month spreads, steady on Wednesday's levels for November/December but three cents wider for December/January and January/February. By early London trading on Thursday the spreads had narrowed three cents.
A December/January Dubai spread was traded at 48 cents late on Wednesday between two European majors.
Paper Tapis for November fell back to a bid of $24.40 from the day-earlier bids of $24.55.
Traders said the decline followed the overnight losses on November Brent of 31 cents to $24.27 and on November NYMEX of 47 cents to $25.07.
The Brent slide continued on SIMEX, with November falling another five cents. London shed another 15 cents by 0930 GMT. --Singapore, N. Fullick (+65 870 3081), Tokyo, Miho Yoshikawa (+813-5473 3706)
